case.title: Miss Victoria Ikolomi v. SGS Scanning Nigeria Limited

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Complaint dated and filed on 7th November 2012.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Trial concluded; parties filed written addresses; judgment delivered.
interlocutory_applications: Order of 4th June 2013 granting claimant leave to amend statement of facts and file additional documents and witness statement on oath.
procedural_events: Claimant filed complaint, statement of facts, witness statement on oath, list of witness, list of documents and copies of documents.
Defendant filed memorandum of appearance, statement of defence, list of witnesses, witness statement on oath, list of documents and copies of documents.
Claimant testified as CW; Emmanuel Idowu Adenipekun testified for defendant as DW.
Parties filed written addresses: defendant's dated 21st January 2014; claimant's dated 20th February 2014 but filed 21st February 2014; defendant's reply on points of law dated 4th March 2014.

material_facts: Claimant and two other staff (Charles Ozah and Ekene Odagu) were queried for breach of audit procedure regarding issuance of Risk Assessment Reports (RARs) for certificate numbers CN/000092432/001 and CN/000092433/001.
The RARs were undervalued, causing lower import duties and loss of revenue to the Federal Government.
Claimant responded to query admitting breach of audit procedure and gross misconduct.
Claimant was summarily dismissed by letter dated 28th August 2012 for corruption.
Claimant accepted terms of dismissal letter, including discharge of defendant from all claims.
Defendant's investigation could not establish that claimant received recharge cards, but assumed she did because two others did.

chronology.event: Claimant and two others allegedly sidetracked procedure for issuance of RARs.
Verbal discussion between claimant and defendant regarding breach.
Claimant summarily dismissed by letter (Exhibit C2/D3).
Claimant signed acceptance of terms of dismissal letter.
Court granted leave to amend statement of facts.

admitted_facts: Claimant admitted breach in response to query.
Claimant accepted terms of dismissal letter.
disputed_facts: Whether breach of audit procedure equates to corruption.
Whether claimant was afforded fair hearing.
Whether claimant received recharge cards or other inducement.
background_facts: Defendant is a company providing scanning services.
Claimant worked as a Ticketing and Reservation Officer with Beverly Travels Ltd at time of trial.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court found that the claimant was queried for breach of audit procedure, which she admitted. The dismissal letter stated corruption, but the court held that breach of audit procedure is not corruption. However, the dismissal was still valid because breach of audit procedure falls under disregard of rules and regulations, which is serious misconduct under clause 15.0(v). The claimant was afforded fair hearing through the query and response. The claimant accepted the terms of the dismissal letter, discharging the defendant from all claims. The claims for damages and solicitor's fees failed.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the claimant is entitled to a declaration that her summary dismissal is illegal, unlawful, null and void; and if so, whether her contract was validly terminated.

arguments.claimant: Dismissal for corruption when queried for breach of audit procedure is illegal and unlawful.
arguments.defendant: Dismissal valid as claimant admitted gross misconduct and was afforded fair hearing.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that corruption is not the same as breach of audit procedure. However, breach of audit procedure is disregard of rules and regulations, which is serious misconduct under clause 15.0(v). The claimant admitted this. Therefore, the dismissal is valid.
issue_analysis.holding: Dismissal is valid; claimant not entitled to declaration.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: An employer can dismiss an employee for serious misconduct, including disregard of rules and regulations, even if the specific label used in the dismissal letter is inaccurate, provided the employee admitted conduct constituting serious misconduct.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the claimant was afforded fair hearing prior to her summary dismissal.

arguments.claimant: Not afforded fair hearing as corruption allegation not put to her.
arguments.defendant: Query and response satisfied fair hearing.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The claimant was queried and responded in writing. This satisfies fair hearing as per Imonikhe v. Unity Bank Plc.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A query given and answered satisfies the requirement of fair hearing in employment disciplinary proceedings.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether having regard to the contract of employment the claimant is entitled to general damages.

arguments.claimant: Entitled to general damages as dismissal letter prejudiced job prospects.
arguments.defendant: Not entitled; no wrongful dismissal; damages limited to salary in lieu of notice.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The dismissal was valid, so no wrongful dismissal. Even if wrongful, general damages not available in ordinary master-servant employment; only salary in lieu of notice.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: In ordinary master-servant employment, damages for wrongful dismissal are limited to salary in lieu of notice; general damages for injured feelings or loss of job prospects are not recoverable.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether having accepted the terms and conditions of the letter of dismissal, the defendant is discharged from all claims, liabilities or obligations.

arguments.claimant: Acceptance does not waive right to challenge dismissal in court.
arguments.defendant: Acceptance discharges defendant from all claims, including court actions.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The terms of the dismissal letter are wide enough to include court actions. The claimant accepted the terms, discharging the defendant from all claims.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A valid agreement discharging an employer from all claims arising from employment bars subsequent court action by the employee.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether having regard to the contract of employment the claimant is entitled to special damages.

arguments.defendant: Not entitled; it is unethical and against public policy.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: Claim for solicitor's fees as special damages fails as it is unethical and against public policy.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A litigant cannot pass on the burden of solicitor's fees to the opponent as special damages.
